title: Coordinated sunsetting of legacy 'compound-generate' endpoint with staged SDK shim and telemetry gates
creator: Asha Varma
description:
Purpose: retire the legacy /v1/compound-generate endpoint (which returned combined generation + embeddings + metadata blobs) in favor of the Unified Inference surface that separates responsibilities (streaming generations, dedicated embeddings, and structured metadata outputs). This ticket defines the PRD-level requirements, scope clarifications, acceptance criteria, SDK shim strategy, telemetry/rollback gates, and the phased timeline for removal.

Goals:
- Ensure minimal customer disruption with automated migration assistance (SDK shim + CLI audit).
- Maintain production SLAs for existing customers during rollout via routing fallbacks and circuit breakers.
- Capture compatibility telemetry to prioritize customers for account outreach.
- Provide clear deprecation messaging and an opt-in extended-support path for enterprise customers.

Out-of-scope:
- Changes to model behavior or default temperature tuning.
- New embedding model versions (will be handled by separate embeddings migration PRD).

Scope clarifications / decisions to date:
- The legacy endpoint will be served in three modes during the window: active (normal behavior), shadow (proxy to new endpoints and compare outputs without returning differences), and header-only (return deprecation headers while still serving).
- SDK shim will translate legacy payloads into one or more calls to the Unified endpoints and reassemble responses to preserve legacy contracts during the shadow phase.
- We will NOT attempt 1:1 model output exact-match acceptance; acceptance is based on functional parity for common usage patterns and a tolerable fuzzy-match threshold for open text.
- Enterprise customers with contractual dependencies can request an extended 12-month paid support window; details handled via CS and legal.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/UG-PRD-CompoundGenerate (draft)
- SDK shim implementation design: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ShimDesign-example
- GitHub shim prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-shims/pull/178
- Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/compound-generate-deprecation

Stakeholders:
- PM: Asha Varma (owner)
- Eng leads: Marco Liu (API), Priya Nair (SDK), Jonas Berg (Runtime)
- DX/Docs: Rachel Kim
- Support & CS: Omar Haddad

Risks and mitigations:
- High-volume customers rely on aggregated responses: offer a migration helper that rewrites requests to parallel calls and provides a merged response; prioritize these accounts for manual outreach.
- Behavioral regressions: run 2 weeks of shadow traffic with automatic anomaly detection on latency, token cost, and semantic drift; pause rollout on any regression beyond defined tolerances.
- SDK adoption lag: provide official 1.0 shim release and a CLI migration audit that can generate code snippets for a customer's codebase.

Acceptance criteria (summary below, full list as separate section):
- SDK shim published and green e2e tests covering top 10 legacy request shapes.
- Shadow mode enabled for at least 30% of production traffic for 14 consecutive days with no severe regressions.
- Telemetry shows migration-ready signal: 95% of unique callers either auto-mapped by shim or flagged for outreach.
- Rollout docs, runbooks, and support playbooks published in docs-redwood by GA date.
acceptance_criteria: Official SDK shim v1.0 released and published to package registries with changelog and migration guide
Automated e2e tests (CI) validate top 10 legacy payload shapes and assert response shape compatibility
Shadow traffic run for >=14 consecutive days with <1% user-facing error delta and latency within 1.5x of baseline for 95% of requests
Telemetry dashboard provides per-customer usage, unmapped request shapes, and semantic-drift alerts
Deprecation header (X-Redwood-Deprecation: compound-generate; removal=2026-09-01) seen by all clients in header-only mode
Customer outreach list generated for any customer with >5% of calls matching unmapped shapes; CS outreach complete before hard removal
Console migration checklist, CLI audit tool, and sample code snippets published under /docs/migration/compound-generate
Rollback playbook and canary abort criteria documented and rehearsed with on-call engineering team

2026-04-15: SDK shim alpha published; invite top 50 customers to trial

2026-06-01: Shadow mode 30% traffic; iterate shim based on findings; CS begins outreach
2026-07-01: Header-only mode for all non-enterprise customers; deprecation headers visible; CLI audit available
2026-08-15: Final cutover window for extended-support customers; last outreach completed
2026-09-01: Hard removal of /v1/compound-generate from public routing; enterprise extended-support windows honored per contract
migration_steps: Publish SDK shim and CLI audit tool; create migration quickstart and sample snippets
Enable shadow proxy that forks requests to Unified endpoints and compares outputs; log diffs
Automated classification job to detect unmapped request shapes and produce account assignment for CS
Run targeted load tests with shim to validate throughput and KV caching behavior under parallelized calls
Update API gateway to inject deprecation headers in header-only mode and configure circuit-breakers
Coordinate with Dedicated & Private teams to ensure private tenants receive same deprecation notice and optional on-prem bundle of shim
Prepare rollback steps: re-enable legacy routing, revoke header-only enforcement, and raise support priority
